knowledge:
- key_parameters: resolution=Sets the HLA allele resolution (e.g., 4 for 4-digit resolution) during import or reduction ;; experiment=Specifies the immunogenetic data transformation type, such as "hla_alleles", "hla_aa", or "hla_NK_ligands" ;; inheritance_model=Specifies the genetic model to test, such as "dominant", "recessive", "overdominant", or "additive" ;; conditional=Logical indicating whether to perform stepwise conditional association testing ;; omnibus=Logical indicating whether to perform a likelihood ratio test grouping residues at each amino acid position ;; lower_frequency_cutoff=Filters out alleles or variables below a specified frequency threshold
- alternatives: None mentioned ;; Use standard R modeling functions (lm, glm, coxme) as the base model for runMiDAS
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing immunogenetic associations using HLA allele calls and/or KIR presence/absence data, particularly for fine-mapping associations to amino acid residues, testing NK cell ligand groups, or evaluating HLA-KIR interactions.
- pitfalls: Phenotypic data read using read.table must include stringsAsFactors = FALSE ;; The statistical model formula must use the placeholder 'term' to represent the tested immunogenetic variable (e.g., disease ~ term) ;; The statistical function used (e.g., glm) must have a tidy method available ;; HLA alleles have complex linkage disequilibrium, so conditional testing should be used to distinguish independent signals from haplotypes

workflows.name: hla_allele_association
workflows.intent: Perform association analysis on classical HLA alleles, filter by Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium, and run conditional testing to identify independent signals.
workflows.stages: 1. Read phenotype data using read.table ;; 2. Read HLA calls using readHlaCalls with a specified resolution ;; 3. Combine genetic and phenotypic data using prepareMiDAS ;; 4. Test for Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium and filter alleles using HWETest ;; 5. Define a statistical model using the placeholder term ;; 6. Run association analysis using runMiDAS ;; 7. Run stepwise conditional association analysis by setting conditional = TRUE in runMiDAS
workflows.code:
dat_pheno <- read.table ( file = system.file ( "extdata" , "MiDAS_tut_pheno.txt" , package = "midasHLA" ), header = TRUE )
dat_HLA <- readHlaCalls ( file = system.file ( "extdata" , "MiDAS_tut_HLA.txt" , package = "midasHLA" ), resolution = 4 )
HLA <- prepareMiDAS ( hla_calls = dat_HLA, colData = dat_pheno, experiment = "hla_alleles" )
HLA <- HWETest ( object = HLA, experiment = "hla_alleles" , HWE_cutoff = 0.05 / 447 , as.MiDAS = TRUE )
HLA_model <- glm (disease ~ term, data = HLA, family = binomial ())
HLA_results <- runMiDAS ( object = HLA_model, experiment = "hla_alleles" , inheritance_model = "dominant" , lower_frequency_cutoff = 0.02 , upper_frequency_cutoff = 0.98 , correction = "bonferroni" , exponentiate = TRUE )
HLA_results_cond <- runMiDAS ( object = HLA_model, experiment = "hla_alleles" , inheritance_model = "dominant" , conditional = TRUE , lower_frequency_cutoff = 0.02 , upper_frequency_cutoff = 0.98 , correction = "bonferroni" , exponentiate = TRUE )

workflows.name: hla_amino_acid_fine_mapping
workflows.intent: Fine-map HLA associations to the amino acid level by inferring residues, running omnibus tests, and mapping residues back to alleles.
workflows.stages: 1. Combine HLA and phenotypic data using prepareMiDAS with experiment = "hla_aa" ;; 2. Define a statistical model using the placeholder term ;; 3. Run a likelihood ratio (omnibus) test using runMiDAS ;; 4. Investigate effect estimates for a specific amino acid position using runMiDAS with omnibus_groups_filter ;; 5. Map amino acid residues back to HLA alleles using getAllelesForAA
workflows.code:
HLA_AA <- prepareMiDAS ( hla_calls = dat_HLA, colData = dat_pheno, experiment = "hla_aa" )
HLA_AA_model <- glm (disease ~ term, data = HLA_AA, family = binomial ())
HLA_AA_omnibus_results <- runMiDAS ( HLA_AA_model, experiment = "hla_aa" , inheritance_model = "dominant" , conditional = FALSE , omnibus = TRUE , lower_frequency_cutoff = 0.02 , upper_frequency_cutoff = 0.98 , correction = "bonferroni" )
HLA_AA_DQB1_ 9 _results <- runMiDAS ( HLA_AA_model, experiment = "hla_aa" , inheritance_model = "dominant" , omnibus_groups_filter = "DQB1_9" , lower_frequency_cutoff = 0.02 , upper_frequency_cutoff = 0.98 , correction = "bonferroni" , exponentiate = TRUE )
HLA_AA_DQB1_ 9 _alleles <- getAllelesForAA (HLA_AA, "DQB1_9" )

workflows.name: hla_kir_interaction_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze associations with Natural Killer (NK) cell ligands and KIR gene presence/absence, including HLA-KIR interactions.
workflows.stages: 1. Combine HLA and phenotypic data using prepareMiDAS with experiment = c("hla_alleles", "hla_NK_ligands") ;; 2. Define a statistical model and run association analysis on NK ligands using runMiDAS ;; 3. Import KIR calls using readKirCalls
workflows.code:
NKlig <- prepareMiDAS ( hla_calls = dat_HLA, colData = dat_pheno, experiment = c ( "hla_alleles" , "hla_NK_ligands" ) )
NKlig_model <- glm (disease ~ term, data = NKlig, family = binomial ())
NKlig_results <- runMiDAS ( NKlig_model, experiment = "hla_NK_ligands" , inheritance_model = "dominant" , correction = "bonferroni" , exponentiate = TRUE )
dat_KIR <- readKirCalls ( file = system.file ( "extdata" , "MiDAS_tut_KIR.txt" , package = "midasHLA" ) )
